thread:
morgan: heads up — after the kernel-selector change landed in staging I'm seeing a measurable perf regression on mixed-precision matmul when activation quantization is enabled. ~25% slower end-to-end on our small-chat microbenchmark :eyes:

alex: can you paste the repro steps and a short profile?

morgan: repro is simple, on dedicated-staging (a100-8):
```
# reproduce
python bench/run_chat.py --model redwood/gpt-13b --seq 512 --batch 1 --quant activate_fp8 --repeat 200
python tools/profile.py --pid $(pgrep -f run_chat.py) --out /tmp/matmul_trace.json
```
profile top lines (wall ms):
```
matmul_mixed_prec_dispatch        1240.3ms
matmul_fp16_kernel                340.1ms
matmul_fp8_kernel                 610.7ms  <-- unexpected hotspot
kv_cache_get                      80.3ms
dispatch/overhead                 210.5ms
```
morgan: interestingly before the selector change fp8 kernel was ~320ms. After change it's ~610ms. KV cache ops also show higher stall time.

tara: did the selector flip which kernel we pick for the (M,N,K) shapes? selector PR mentioned a throughput model change but not layout changes.

morgan: yes — autotuner now prefers the FP8 path for our common (1024, 4096, 4096) pattern. But I instrumented cache behavior: kv_cache_hit_rate dropped from 0.86 -> 0.63 when fp8 path used. Seems packing/stride differences cause cache-line misalignment and prefetch inefficiency.

sam: that matches something I saw — FP8 packer changed tensor layout to optimize vectorized stores (8-bit lanes) which increases stride for KV rows. On A100 that increases L2 miss rate for the KV prefetch pattern. Did you get L1/L2 stats?

morgan: yep. L2 miss rate jumped 14% -> 28%. Also more PCIe memory copies in traces (we're near host-bound for small batches).

peter: any correctness issues? usually quant changes cause small FP perturbations but not huge perf hits.

morgan: unit tests pass, but I found occasional output divergence for long-context decoding when activation quant + fp8 is used: token-level diffs appear after ~200 tokens. Not NaNs, just noisy softmax differences causing different argmax.

alex: can you post a tiny example that reproduces correctness divergence? we can add to regression tests.

morgan: short repro attached (pasting prompt snippet):
```
# seeds identical
prompt = "The quick brown fox" * 20
out_fp16 = run_model(prompt, prec='fp16', activation_quant=False)
out_fp8 = run_model(prompt, prec='fp8', activation_quant=True)
# compare first 256 tokens
assert out_fp16[:256] != out_fp8[:256]  # shows divergence around token 210
```

sam: that explains why tests missed it — numeric tolerance checks only compared logprobs within 1e-3 and for short prefixes. We need a long-sequence, greedy-decoding exact-match test across precisions.

morgan: my hypothesis: misaligned packing + increased KV stalls changes scheduling and micro-batching timing; combined with slightly different rounding in FP8 matmul results in drift that compounds during autoregressive decode. So root isn't just math, it's timing + cache-induced variation.

perf-bot: autometrics report attached — rolling-avg latency bumped 22% on canary, p95 increased 1.8x.

tara: immediate mitigation options:
- revert kernel-selector autotuner change (fast, blunt)
- force-int8 for small-seq shapes while we investigate (narrow scope)
- modify fp8 packer to preserve previous stride/padding (longer dev)

alex: prefer force-int8 for sequence_len <= 128 and revert autotuner in staging until we have a fix. Canary rollback if needed.

peter: also add an end-to-end regression test: decode 512 tokens greedy on a deterministic prompt and assert token parity across fp16/fp8 with activation-quant enabled. Put it in eng-runtime/regressions.

sam: I'll own the packer fix prototype (align padding to 64B) — should reduce L2 misses. If packer can't meet perf we might need a small kernel variant tuned for the new layout.

morgan: assigned: @alex revert autotuner in staging, @sam prototype packer alignment, @peter add regression test, @tara coordinate canary rollback if latency spikes. I'll dump the full perf traces and a reproducible docker image to the bug ticket (INF-8432).

alex: doing revert now. rolling back selector change on staging and launching a canary release to validate.

morgan: thanks — after revert I'll rerun bench and post updated numbers. If anyone wants the raw traces DM me, they're ~12MB zipped. :thumbsup:

sam: FYI I'll also run a microbenchmark matrix crossing batch sizes [1,4,8], seq_len [64,128,512], and kernels [fp16,fp8,int8] and push CSV to the perf bucket so we can tune heuristics instead of blind autotune.

peter: and I'll add the long-decode regression to CI with a nightly slower job so we catch flakies early.

morgan: update — after revert, p95 and p50 back to baseline on staging. Regression ticket INF-8432 updated with trace, L2 stats, and suggested fixes. Closing loop here unless anyone objects. :white_check_mark:
